_comment: Shared Skeleton pulse vectors. Read by coui_core (CoreColor.scaleAlpha),
coui_flutter (the alpha the widget paints) and coui_web (the --pulse-from
/ --pulse-to it emits) tests, so a pulse that drifts on one platform fails
against the same numbers the other two produce.
The pulse opacity is MULTIPLIED into the fill's own alpha: restAlpha is
fill alpha x fromOpacity, peakAlpha is fill alpha x toOpacity. A raw fill
rounds to a whole alpha byte (CoreColor.scaleAlpha), which is why
0x33000000 rests at 26/255 rather than 25.5/255.
fill: null is the variant default (an opaque token); {token, opacity} is a
token fill; {argb} is a raw fill. Token fills assume an opaque scheme
colour, which every CoUI preset is.
Where the pulse is at a point in its period. Read by coui_core (the
Core default and a cubic-bezier evaluation), coui_flutter (the alpha
the controller paints at that time) and coui_web (the period, curve
and keyframes it emits). `t` is the fraction of one full pulse, rest
-> peak -> rest; `progress` is 0 at the rest end and 1 at the peak, so
the painted alpha is restAlpha + (peakAlpha - restAlpha) x progress.
Each half eases FORWARD with the curve (rest -> peak, then peak ->
rest), the way a CSS timing function applies per keyframe interval.
The second case uses an asymmetric curve: a symmetric one (the
default) reads the same played forward or backward, so it could not
tell the two apart.
